{
  "question_intent": "Requesting clarification on capital generation targets, distributions, and TNAV growth.",
  "main_topics": ["capital generation targets", "distributions", "TNAV growth"],
  "answer_completeness": "Partial",
  "response_stance": "Hedged",
  "evidence_level": "Medium",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Partially aligned",
  "question_quote": "If I can take it up a level, if that's okay, got a couple of questions. I'm really trying to triangulate the capital generation targets on slide 71 and with the RoTE and the distribution expectations. I mean, greater than 230 basis points on circa £400 billion of RWA is obviously getting you to an attributable profit number of over £9 billion. So putting to one side, that's quite a bit ahead of consensus, even if we assume 3% RWA growth, which if the Investment Bank is pretty flat is quite a lot. That's only going to take us down to about £8 billion of free capital generation, which is obviously huge in the context of the £15 billion plus over the three years. So can I just firstly ask do you recognise those numbers, are these distributions going to be really quite back-end loaded such that when you are stood here in two years' time, the next three years of distributions are going to be markedly above the greater than £15 billion that you've talked about today. Secondly, connected, the RoTE on that 230 basis points plus, if we use consensus TNAV would be closer to 15%, maybe a little above 15%. I just wonder if you can talk to TNAV growth over the next few years would be great if you can reference consensus, but maybe some of the things that are harder for us to model like the own credit unwind, the pension surplus, maybe even the cash flow hedge reserve moves to a positive. How should we be thinking about TNAV two or three years forward, please, particularly versus consensus. Thank you.",
  "answer_quote": "Thanks, Jonathan. I guess both of those are for me. So let me just start with capital. So, I'm not going to comment on your maths, Jonathan. Where I agree with you is that the organisation is generating a lot of capital and we expect that to continue. So when we give you a distribution target of greater than £15 billion, I would concentrate on two things within that slide. One is the greater than sign. And the second is this point that we are making that beyond the investment that we've got in the plan, so beyond the doubling of investment and beyond the level of distributions, there is an element of capital creation here that we are holding for additional investment if we think that is the right thing to do. Now if we don't, then we will, of course, return that to shareholders. That's what our capital hierarchy says. It says, first, be well-capitalised, then deliver it to shareholders, then invest it to meaningfully improve the returns of the Group. So that capital hierarchy remains. We have no desire to hold on to excess levels of capital. Your thought process is as ours is, but as I say, I will leave the maths to you. Last time I looked at it, our expectations of TNAV versus consensus TNAV were broadly similar.",
  "question_intent": "Requesting clarification on capital generation targets, distributions, and TNAV growth.",
  "main_topics": ["capital generation targets", "distributions", "TNAV growth"],
  "answer_completeness": "Partial",
  "response_stance": "Hedged",
  "evidence_level": "Medium",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Partially aligned",
  "reason": "The answer partially addresses the question by discussing capital generation and TNAV growth but does not provide specific details on distributions or TNAV growth projections."
}
